cases.prompt: Design the UI for our new product.
expect: Asks whether it is a portal, a landing page, a storefront, or a mix before proposing screens
must_not: Assumes an admin dashboard layout without asking

cases.prompt: Design the UI for a gym membership app.
expect: Proposes a screen map with screens, actors, and the main flow
Asks only the decisions that block the design (platform, navigation, brand) through the host's choice tool
Ends the turn after asking
must_not: Writes page or component code before the decisions are answered
Asks about things the kit already decides, such as the component library or icon set

expect: Reads the feature spec, actors, domain model, and business rules first
Maps every screen to the journeys and requirements it covers
Designs loading, empty, error, and no-permission states for each screen
must_not: Adds screens or fields that no requirement asks for without marking them as proposals
Invents API endpoints

cases.prompt: Set up the UI for our new Next.js monorepo and build a dashboard page.
expect: Copies the Base UI React kit into packages/ui from vaultia-templates
Wires theme.css, data-theme, and the locale provider into the app
Builds the dashboard in the app by composing kit components
Runs typecheck and build
must_not: Re-creates buttons, inputs, dialogs, or tables inside the app
Rewrites the kit from memory when it cannot be downloaded

cases.prompt: Add a settings page to our app. We already use MUI.
expect: Uses MUI components and the existing theme
Applies the UX planning and checklist
must_not: Installs the Base UI React kit or replaces MUI without the user asking

cases.prompt: Change the primary color to our brand green #16A34A and support dark mode.
expect: Edits the brand scale in tokens.json and regenerates the theme CSS with the build script
Checks primary-foreground contrast in light and dark mode
must_not: Hard-codes hex colors or palette classes in components or screens
Edits the generated theme CSS by hand

cases.prompt: Review our orders page for UX problems.
expect: Reports findings ranked Blocking, Important, Minor with screen, problem, and fix
Asks before making changes
must_not: Rewrites the page before reporting

cases.prompt: Thiết kế giao diện màn hình danh sách hợp đồng cho admin.
expect: Replies in Vietnamese
Proposes the screen layout and states before building
Uses the Vietnamese UI locale or the project's i18n for screen text
must_not: Hard-codes Vietnamese text inside kit components

cases.prompt: Build a landing page for our scheduling SaaS. Goal: book a demo.
expect: Treats the page as design-led: distinctive layout, typography, and motion
Uses one primary call to action (book a demo) repeated down the page
Proposes sections such as hero, social proof, benefits, how it works, pricing or FAQ, final CTA
Plans static or server rendering, SEO metadata, and a mobile performance budget
Builds sections in the app from kit components and tokens
Keeps content readable without animation and respects reduced motion
must_not: Uses an app shell with a sidebar or dense tables
Invents customer logos, testimonials, or numbers presented as real
Ships lorem ipsum

cases.prompt: Design the product page and checkout for our online clothing store.
expect: Keeps content clear and specific with motion limited to hover and feedback
Shows price, variants, stock, delivery, and returns on the product page
Offers guest checkout and shows the full cost before the final step
Keeps the cart and input when payment fails
Plans Product and Offer structured data and server rendering for product pages
must_not: Forces account creation before purchase
Adds commerce components such as the product card or cart to the kit package
Adds decorative animations that delay browsing or buying

cases.prompt: We need a storefront plus a customer account area with order history.
expect: applies the storefront rules to shopping pages and the portal rules to the account area
must_not: Uses one set of patterns for both

cases.prompt: Build the contract management screens for our rental admin portal.
expect: Focuses on business rules, statuses, permissions, and edge cases from the requirements
Uses kit defaults with just-enough visuals and functional motion only
Designs dense interactions: table, filters, row and bulk actions, forms
must_not: Adds decorative imagery, hero sections, or scroll animations
